angleEvidenceBrief: All 186 municipalities were sent and all 186 came back: GET /v3/charts/yNwL8/data returns 187 lines, 186 rows, the 6 unanswered municipalities still blank and the maximum still 104.2. Nothing was truncated or sampled. The delivered PNG was opened at 1920x1080 and again at 1080x1920: the cloud is flat across the whole household range (Pearson r = -0.07 over the 180 municipalities that answered), the dashed rule at 100 per cent renders with its paired label, and Commune-063 sits visibly above it with its own annotation. The takeaway the chart carries is the one the data can settle; the article own regional claim is not, and the storyboard says why.
reviewer: the journalist (this run: the decision was taken on their behalf, see the report for this stress round)
notes: Approved with two limitations recorded rather than waved through. (1) THE HOUSE ACCENT DID NOT REACH THE MARKS. spec.color is #5B8A8A; the 186 dots in the delivered PNG are #18a1cd, Datawrapper own default blue, read straight off the bytes (2014 pixels of #18a1cd against 1811 of #5B8A8A, and the #5B8A8A pixels are all rule and label). buildChartPayload only sets visualize[base-color] when isBarEncoded(chartType) matches /bars|column/, so a scatter is left with custom-colors alone - the exact key round three measured as inert. (2) THE X AXIS RUNS TO -4,000 HOUSEHOLDS at landscape. computeYRange fits the y axis and there is no x equivalent, so the household axis keeps Datawrapper own padded default and states a quantity that cannot exist. At portrait the same chart draws 0-50,000 and the defect disappears, which is how it was isolated. Neither is a data error and both ship visible.
